title: Line Plots with Fractions
short: Make line plots in eighths and add or subtract with them.

blocks.html: In Grade 3 you made line plots with halves and fourths. Now the measurements go to eighths of an inch, and you can use adding and subtracting like fractions to answer questions about them.

A line plot puts an X above a number line for each measurement. Stacks show how many times a value happened. To find the difference between the longest and shortest, subtract the values at the two ends; to combine pieces, add their values.
Every measurement keeps its exact place on the scale, so you can read the data and still do math with it. Counting X marks tells you "how many," and the numbers under them tell you "how long."

blocks.name: g4-lineplot

opts.label: length of a leaf, in inches

blocks.cap: Leaf lengths in eighths of an inch. Tap above the scale to add a measurement, or tap the top X to remove one; the line under the plot updates.

blocks.title: Difference
blocks.q: Using the plot, what is the difference between the longest and shortest leaf?

blocks.title: Combine equal pieces
blocks.q: If all the $\dfrac{5}{8}$-inch leaves were laid end to end, how long would they be?

blocks.html: Counting the X marks when the question asks for a length, or using the number of a stack as a measurement. Ask: does the question want "how many" (count X marks) or "how long" (use the scale values)?

sources.name: Common Core State Standards for Mathematics, Grade 4, 4.MD.B.4 (make a line plot of measurements in fractions of a unit and solve problems using it)
